Pipeline stage: test security

Source: R/pipeline-security.R
check_security.Rd

Looks for evidence that a score may not reflect the test taker's own ability, before scores are reported. Each check runs when the data it needs are there. Security flags are evidence for an investigation, not proof of misconduct, so the respondents involved are kept in p$security$persons and never appear in score reports; flags and the report give counts only.

Usage

check_security(p, leaked = NULL, window = NULL, site = NULL, prior = NULL)

Arguments

p

a calibrated pipeline.

leaked

optional item ids suspected to be leaked or exposed.

window

optional administration window of each respondent (in time order: numbers, dates, or an ordered factor).

site

optional site, school or classroom of each respondent.

prior

optional earlier scores: a data frame with columns id, theta and optionally se, on the same scale.

Value

The pipeline with p$security: persons (respondent-level evidence, for investigators only), and tables for the item checks.

Details

The checks (thresholds from mv_rules()):

  • preknowledge (review): with leaked items named, test takers who do much better on the leaked items than on the secure ones (likelihood ratio test of one ability against separate abilities for the two sets, p below preknowledge_alpha, leaked ability higher).

  • item_leakage (review): with window given, items whose proportion correct rose by more than leak_p in the latest window compared with the earlier ones and, when response times are available, whose median time fell by more than leak_rt.

  • parameter_drift (review): with an item bank, items whose difficulty (or slope) on the bank scale moved more than drift_b (drift_a) from the bank value.

  • answer_copying (review): pairs of test takers who share far more identical incorrect answers than expected from their scores (Poisson tail probability below copy_alpha after a Bonferroni correction over all pairs). Needs raw responses scored with a key.

  • aberrant_timing (review): test takers whose response times are much shorter than expected (standardized log-time residual below rt_resid on at least rt_share of the items, from a lognormal model with item time intensities and person speeds; fit_rt() fits the full model).

  • site_anomaly (review): with site given, sites or classrooms with a larger share of flagged test takers than chance allows (binomial test, p below site_alpha).

  • score_gain (info): with prior scores, gains above gain_sem times the standard error of the difference.

Examples

# \donttest{
p <- add_responses(mv_pipeline(), certexam, items = 3:34, key = certexam_key, id = "id")
p <- calibrate(drop_items(p, "Q14"), model = "2PL")
p <- check_security(p, leaked = c("Q01", "Q02", "Q03", "Q04", "Q05"))
#> Warning: Test security is running with 1 review open flag(s) from earlier stages:
#>   #2 [review] local_dependence: Q21 & Q22 (Q3 = 0.27)
#> Flags only warn because strict = FALSE. See flags(p).
flags(p, stage = "security")
#> # A tibble: 0 × 10
#> # ℹ 10 variables: id <int>, stage <chr>, check <chr>, target <chr>,
#> #   value <chr>, rule <chr>, level <chr>, advice <chr>, status <chr>,
#> #   note <chr>
# }
